summary: Sublingual nitroglycerin is a fast-acting organic nitrate used to relieve or acutely prevent angina pectoris attacks due to coronary artery disease. It works by releasing nitric oxide, which dilates veins (reducing preload) and, at higher doses, arteries. It is contraindicated with PDE-5 inhibitors and sGC stimulators because of severe hypotension. A patient with chest pain that does not resolve after 3 tablets should seek emergency care.
indications: Acute relief of an angina pectoris attack due to coronary artery disease
Acute prophylaxis of angina before activities likely to precipitate an attack

dosage.d: 1 tablet under the tongue or in the buccal pouch at first sign of attack; allow to dissolve
dosage.n: May repeat every 5 minutes; no more than 3 tablets in 15 minutes

dosage.d: 1 tablet 5-10 minutes before activity likely to precipitate angina
If pain persists after 3 tablets over 15 minutes, seek emergency care
dosage.n: Atypical pain also warrants prompt evaluation

admin: Place one tablet under the tongue or in the buccal pouch and allow it to dissolve; do not swallow or chew
Sit or lie down before taking due to risk of dizziness/fainting
For dry mouth, a small sip of water beforehand may aid dissolution
Keep tablets in the original tightly closed glass container; replace per expiry
Call emergency services if pain persists after 3 tablets in 15 minutes
moa: Nitroglycerin is denitrated to release free radical nitric oxide (NO), which activates guanylate cyclase and increases intracellular cyclic GMP in vascular smooth muscle. This dephosphorylates myosin light chains and relaxes smooth muscle, producing venous dilation (reduced preload) and, at higher doses, arterial dilation, decreasing myocardial oxygen demand and relieving angina.

absolute: Concurrent PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, avanafil)
Hypersensitivity to nitrates/nitrites or any excipient

preg: Limited human data; use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether sublingual nitroglycerin is excreted in human milk; use with caution and weigh maternal need against potential infant risk.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is required.

major: PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, avanafil): life-threatening hypotension - contraindicated
Soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat): severe hypotension - contraindicated
moderate: Antihypertensives, vasodilators, and other nitrates (additive hypotension)
Heparin (nitroglycerin may reduce its anticoagulant effect)
interactions.food: Not related to meals; dissolve under the tongue.
interactions.diagnostics: High doses may cause methemoglobinemia, affecting pulse oximetry/blood gas readings.

monitoring: Headache as a common dose-limiting effect
Signs of nitrate tolerance with frequent use
counsel: Sit down before taking a tablet to avoid fainting
If chest pain is not relieved after 3 tablets over 15 minutes, call emergency services
Headache is common and usually eases with continued use
Never use with erectile dysfunction drugs (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil)
Store in the original glass container, tightly closed; tablets lose potency over time
pk: Original tightly closed glass container at 20-25 C; protect from heat/moisture
pearls: Fast-acting rescue therapy for acute angina; carry tablets at all times
Absolutely contraindicated with PDE-5 inhibitors due to fatal hypotension risk
Continuous/frequent use causes nitrate tolerance; maintain a nitrate-free interval for long-acting forms
Persistent pain after 3 tablets may signal myocardial infarction - seek emergency care
missed: This is a rescue/as-needed medication, not a scheduled dose, so there is no missed-dose schedule. Use only at the onset of an attack or before precipitating activity as directed.
overdose: Overdose causes severe hypotension, reflex tachycardia, throbbing headache, flushing, syncope, and methemoglobinemia. Treat by elevating the legs, giving IV fluids, and supporting blood pressure; avoid epinephrine. Methemoglobinemia is treated with intravenous methylene blue.
